correctness.rationale: Thaddeus gives the exact sequence definition of complete skew forms and a smooth projective blow-up model. With binary-separated diagonal weights, all coordinate wedge weights are distinct. Hence the first fixed projective two-form is one coordinate wedge, its kernel is the complementary coordinate subspace, and induction repeats the same argument on that kernel. This gives a bijection between fixed points and ordered pairings of the coordinate labels, leaving one singleton only in odd dimension. The resulting product of pair choices is exactly the claimed factorial quotient. Bialynicki--Birula decomposition then identifies the Euler characteristic with this isolated fixed-point count. The packaged checker independently enumerates ordered matchings in small dimensions and verifies the exact recurrence over a much larger range.

value.rationale: Complete skew forms are a classical wonderful compactification and form the antisymmetric member of the complete-forms triad. The theorem gives a closed topological invariant in every dimension and identifies it with a natural ordered-matching count. The formula is structurally informative because it sharply contrasts with the companion complete-quadrics and complete-collineations Euler laws: the antisymmetric fixed-point geometry produces a single factorial divided by a power of two. This is an all-dimension classification of a canonical invariant, not a routine finite computation.
